As for SQL Server, go to PostgreSQL. You'll find it generally performs better than SQL Server and has many more options. Should you outgrow PostgreSQL there are many commercial options allowing for both horizontal and vertical growth.

Your quest to find a per language IDE is a mistake. You're a very experienced developer and it's time to invest in yourself as such. Learn EMACS and/or VIM. Or a hybrid environment of something like Spacemacs. Once you get past the initial wall you'll wonder why you ever spent time in VS. In fact, it will seem down right primitive and slow in comparison. These tools are available on ever platform and are far more powerful, extensible, and advanced that VS. VS's hook is that it integrates very well with .NET and it's expansion capabilities helps with the learning curve of new frameworks. But after 17 years of development you should no longer need the training wheels. If you do, you need some time for introspection. ;)

Learn to use git. You'll never want to look at anything else afterwards.

Don't be fooled by comments like, "slow emacs startup." If this is an issue for you, you're using it wrong. Learn about daemon mode. Learn about TRAMP (edit remote files as if they are local) and learn about dired and VC modes. The learning curve is tall but the power is immense in comparison to basic tools like VS.

alias edit='emacsclient -c'

Learn basic VI skills too. Learn about nano and VIM.

PS. MySQL is a terrible database platform. Unless required to do so, stay away from it. It only became popular because people who don't know anything about RDBMSs liked it. Even today, it scales terribly, assuming you want ACID.

If you really want to jump into EMACS, learn about calender, diary, and especially the super awesome Org mode.

Many people lean toward VIM because it's easier to learn. But EMACS still remains the master of all IDEs.

BTW, there are also several PostgreSQL modes for EMACS too. You can type your queries directly in emacs and run them against PostgreSQL.

If you invest in yourself in learning these advanced tools, your entire development life will change for the better.

Intro to Org mode: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SzA2YODtgK4 TRAMP mode: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iqh50fgbIVk Some emacs videos: https://www.youtube.com/user/emacsrocks
